terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of a solid ionic compound is formed from its gaseous ions.
terms.examiner: Exothermic. Lattice dissociation is the reverse: one mole of the solid is separated into gaseous ions, and has the same value with the opposite sign.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous atoms is formed from an element in its standard state.
terms.examiner: For chlorine it is ½Cl₂(g) → Cl(g), which is half the bond dissociation enthalpy.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous atoms gains one mole of electrons to form one mole of gaseous 1− ions.
terms.examiner: The first is usually exothermic; the second is endothermic because an electron is added to an ion that is already negative.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of gaseous ions is converted into aqueous ions.
terms.examiner: Always exothermic; more exothermic for small, highly charged ions.

terms.definition: The enthalpy change when one mole of an ionic solid dissolves in enough water that the ions are well separated and do not interact.
terms.examiner: Enthalpy of solution = lattice dissociation enthalpy + the sum of the hydration enthalpies.

terms.definition: A measure of the disorder of a system.
terms.examiner: Gases have much higher entropy than liquids or solids; more moles of gas in the products means ΔS is positive.

terms.definition: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS. A reaction is feasible when ΔG is zero or negative.
terms.examiner: Convert ΔS from J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ to kJ K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ before using it with ΔH.

terms.definition: Ions are treated as point charges, or perfect spheres, with only electrostatic attraction between them.
terms.examiner: A Born–Haber lattice enthalpy larger than the theoretical value shows some covalent character.
